_what: Batch 160 preparation, data only: one row per table in `app` and `private`, the §5 retention class each sits under, whether §10 defines it, what a sweep would read, §10's final behaviour, what blocks that behaviour today and the open decisions it needs. NO NUMBER from §10 is encoded here as a value: §10's numbers are unapproved (ERD:484) and §15 forbids an agent choosing an open decision. A class §10 does not define is a FINDING, never a number.
_measured: The table set, columns, indexes, UPDATE/DELETE privileges, triggers and foreign keys were read from a clean `make db-migrate-clean` at 75c9274 (PostgreSQL 17.11, 127.0.0.1:5511, shim first) and are re-derived from the migration text by test-kits/db/foundation-contract.test.mjs on every run, so this file cannot silently describe a schema that no longer exists.

_shape.table: schema-qualified table a migration creates; exactly one row each
_shape.section5: the §5 inventory row (ERD line) the table sits under, its cells verbatim
_shape.section9_classes: §9.1 classes this table carries, each picked from §5's sensitivity cell
_shape.section10_class: the §10 class, or null when none can be given (then class_status is `finding`)
_shape.sweeps: each predicate a sweep would read: its key columns, its basis (never a number), and the indexes whose leading columns cover the key (empty = not covered; a partial index is named too, and its predicate is not read here)
_shape.final_behaviour: §10's final behaviour reduced to purge / anonymise / retain; the verbatim text is in section10_classes
_shape.blocking_controls: what refuses that behaviour today. Kinds: no-delete-grant, no-update-grant, client-only-update, grant-without-policy, trigger, no-schema-usage. controls_on_every_row hold for all rows.
_shape.decisions: open decision ids the row needs: DATA-DEC-04..10 (ERD:867-873) and Q160-a..d (the 141-170 phase plan)

controls_on_every_row.what: No service identity exists: RFC-2026-022 is NOT IN EFFECT (the only member of app_worker is postgres), no policy anywhere names app_worker, app_maintenance, app_command or service_role, and app_maintenance holds no privilege on any table.
§10's precedence puts a hold first (ERD:516-526) and no hold table exists (open_blockers[120] ("no legal-hold table")).
The immutable object-deletion manifest has no home or owner (open_blockers[150] ("HAS NO HOME IN THIS REPOSITORY"); CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md:47).

No multipart or temporary-upload table exists.
app.outbox_events would carry it, but §5 assigns `JOB-SHORT/LEDGER` (F160-05).
app.consumer_ledger would carry it, but §5 assigns `JOB-SHORT/LEDGER` (F160-05).

findings.what: §5 assigns connector.meta `CONNECTION-HISTORY`; §10 defines no such class.
findings.source: ERD:211; ERD:488-514; open_blockers[4] ("DEFINES NO SUCH CLASS")

findings.what: §5 assigns industry.core `CATALOG/HISTORY`; §10 defines no `CATALOG`, and `HISTORY` ("immutable ... versions", "อายุ Workspace + lineage") cannot describe a global catalog row, nor a mutable business assignment.
findings.source: ERD:204; ERD:490; open_blockers[77] ("§10 DEFINES NO `CATALOG` CLASS**. Its table has twenty-seven rows")

findings.what: §5's glob `NOTIFICATION-*` does not reach §10's `PUSH-SECRET`, the class written for this table. The class is DEFINED in §10 (row 21); the finding is the assignment, not the definition.
The glob reaches only `NOTIFICATION-INBOX` ("user notifications", 180 days, purge), which does not describe a preference row; no §10 class does.
findings.source: ERD:215; ERD:507; open_blockers[192] ("(1) F160-04: §5's NOTIFICATION-* reaches only NOTIFICATION-INBOX")

findings.what: §10 defines no `LEDGER`; it defines `OUTBOX-SHORT` and `CONSUMER-LEDGER`, which §5 does not name. Batch 050 recorded it and encoded nothing.

The glob `AI-RUN-*` matches no §10 class literally (§10 has `AI-RUN` and `AI-RAW`), both describe runs, and no generation-run table exists; neither describes the global model registry, a workspace model policy or a credential reference.

The glob `ASSET-*` reaches `ASSET-ORIGINAL` and `ASSET-DERIVATIVE` only. Batch 100 reads it as also covering `RIGHTS-PROOF` and `UPLOAD-TEMP` (100_asset.sql:421-423), which the glob does not match; and no §10 class describes a content-asset link row.

§5 puts billing.core under `FINANCE-HISTORY`, while §10's `WEBHOOK-SHORT` names the "raw Meta/payment webhook inbox" in its data column. Batch 131 read the receipt as WEBHOOK-SHORT; the two documents disagree about this table, and WEBHOOK-SHORT's two-speed behaviour degenerates because the receipt stores no payload.
findings.source: ERD:218; ERD:502; open_blockers[105] ("BATCH 131 ENCODES NEITHER NUMBER")

findings.what: app.workspaces carries lifecycle_state and no timestamp of entering a state, so the 30-day recovery window (DATA-DEC-04) has no column to measure from; updated_at moves on any update.
app.jobs has no terminal-state column or timestamp, so JOB-SHORT's "30 วัน success; 90 วัน failed/DLQ" split cannot be swept; there is no attempts or DLQ table.
SCHEDULE-HISTORY is "12 เดือนหลัง final state" and neither app.calendar_items nor app.content_schedules records when a final state was reached.
findings.source: ERD:497; 091_calendar.sql:59; open_blockers[190] ("records WHEN its final state was reached")

findings.what: RESEARCH-RUN is "12 เดือนหลัง last use" and app.research_runs has no last-use column (used_at is on suggestions only); completed_at is the nearest column and it is not indexed.

Sweep keys with no covering index, measured: see every row whose sweeps[].covered_by is empty (13 keys). Two more are covered only by a partial index whose predicate excludes the rows the sweep reads (sweeps[].partial_cover.verdict = F160-13): workspace_invitations.expires_at (pending only) and billing_webhook_receipts.received_at (unprocessed only). Fifteen in all.

Rows §10 retains hold foreign keys to rows §10 purges (see purge-order.json retention_conflicts); with every FK NO ACTION, the parent cannot be purged while the retained child exists. In particular app.workspaces cannot be hard-deleted while FINANCE-HISTORY rows reference it. Twelve is a LOWER BOUND: the rule needs a behaviour on both ends of a key, finding rows have none, and 21 non-self keys touch a finding row (measured); the count can grow when Q160-c is answered.

app.assets and app.asset_versions reference each other (assets_current_version_scope_fk and asset_versions_asset_scope_fk); the purge must null assets.current_version_id first, an UPDATE only app_worker holds a grant for and no policy admits.
findings.source: live catalog FKs; open_blockers[192] ("(11) F160-15: the app.assets <-> app.asset_versions cycle")

findings.what: §10's `HISTORY` data column names knowledge and content versions, which §5 puts under `CONTENT-HISTORY`; both end in a purge, so the disagreement changes no behaviour today.

§5 gives app.workspace_invitations TOKEN-SHORT (purge), while §10 AUTH-HISTORY's data column names "invitations history" (anonymise actor fields, retain a security minimum). The two classes disagree on the final behaviour; the map keeps §5's TOKEN-SHORT and decides nothing, in particular not whether accepted invitations are AUTH-HISTORY.
